objectives.text: Recognise and describe food and nutrition facts and principles
Explain food and nutrition ideas and problems
Generate solutions to provide data to determine the feasibility of the solution
Evaluate and refine ideas and solutions to make justified recommendations for enhancement
Make decisions about and use mode-appropriate features, language and conventions for particular purposes and contexts

unit_structure.title: Food science of vitamins, minerals and protein
unit_structure.description: Students explore sectors of the food system and the nutrients that make up our food. They explore fundamentals of food science through practical investigation of the nutritional and scientific properties of vitamins, minerals and protein in foods. Students use the Food & Nutrition problem-solving process to build knowledge and develop and test ideas using a range of experimental techniques to create solutions.
objectives: Recognise and describe facts and principles related to the nutritional, chemical, functional and sensory properties of vitamins, minerals and protein-based food
Explain food science ideas and problems related to vitamins, minerals and protein-based food
Analyse problems, information and data related to the properties and processing of vitamins, minerals and protein-based food
Determine success criteria for vitamin, mineral and protein-based food problems
Synthesise information and data for vitamin, mineral and protein-based food solutions
Generate vitamin, mineral or protein-based food solutions to provide data to determine the feasibility of the solution
Evaluate and refine ideas and solutions to make justified recommendations for modification or enhancement of vitamin, mineral and protein-based food solutions
Make decisions about and use mode-appropriate features, language and conventions for particular purposes and food and nutrition contexts

unit_structure.title: Food drivers and emerging trends
unit_structure.description: Students explore the factors that determine what food solutions will be developed and made ready for marketing and consumption. These factors include consumer drivers and quality control standards, including food safety and labelling legislation.
objectives: Recognise and describe facts and principles related to consumer demand, labelling and food safety
Explain ideas and problems related to current and emerging consumer food markets
Analyse problems, information and data related to current and emerging consumer food markets and food safety problems
Determine success criteria for emerging consumer market and food safety problems
Synthesise information and data to develop ideas for solutions related to emerging consumer market and food safety problems
Generate consumer market and food safety food solutions to provide data to determine the feasibility of the solution
Evaluate and refine ideas and solutions to make justified recommendations for modification or enhancement of consumer market and food safety food solutions
Make decisions about and use mode-appropriate features, language and conventions for particular purposes and food and nutrition contexts

unit_structure.title: Food science of carbohydrate and fat
unit_structure.description: Students develop knowledge about the chemical, functional and sensory properties of carbohydrate- and fat-based food, and food safety, food preservation techniques and spoilage.
objectives: Recognise and describe facts and principles related to the nutritional, chemical, functional and sensory properties of carbohydrate- and fat-based food
Explain food science ideas and problems related to carbohydrate- and fat-based food
Analyse problems, information and data related to the properties and processing of carbohydrate- and fat-based food
Determine success criteria for carbohydrate- and fat-based food problems
Synthesise information and data for carbohydrate- and fat-based food solutions
Generate carbohydrate- and fat-based food solutions to provide data to determine the feasibility of the solution
Evaluate and refine ideas and solutions to make justified recommendations for modification or enhancement of carbohydrate- and fat-based food solutions
Make decisions about and use mode-appropriate features, language and conventions for particular purposes and food and nutrition contexts

unit_structure.title: Food solution development for nutrition consumer markets
unit_structure.description: Students focus on the investigation of problems for nutrition consumer markets and develop solutions for these while improving safety, nutrition, transparency and accessibility, as well as considering the wider impacts and implications of solutions.
objectives: Recognise and describe facts and principles related to nutrition consumer markets and food solution development
Explain ideas and problems related to nutrition consumer markets
Analyse problems, information and data related to nutrition consumer markets
Determine success criteria for nutrition consumer market problems
Synthesise information and data to develop ideas for nutrition consumer market solutions
Generate nutrition consumer market solutions to provide data to determine the feasibility of the solution
Evaluate and refine ideas and solutions to make justified recommendations for modification or enhancement of nutrition consumer market solutions
Make decisions about and use mode-appropriate features, language and conventions for particular purposes and food and nutrition contexts

units_1_2.description: Schools develop at least two but no more than four assessments; complete at least one assessment for each unit; ensure each unit objective is assessed at least once. Schools make judgments using reporting standards or instrument-specific marking guides (ISMGs). Marks not required for QCAA reporting.
units_1_2.reporting: Satisfactory (S) or unsatisfactory (U); may also report not rated (NR)

units_3_4.description: Three internal assessments using QCAA-provided specifications and conditions, plus one external assessment developed and marked by QCAA.

internal_assessments.name: Food & Nutrition solution

units_3_4.reporting: Provisional criterion marks reported to QCAA; confirmed results combined with external assessment for subject result out of 100 and A–E
